entities.summary: Mas‘ud ibn Muhammad Sijzi was a prominent Persian physician of the 14th century who made significant contributions to the field of medicine in eastern Iran. He was born in the city of Nishapur, Khorasan, during the rule of the Timurid Empire and later moved to the court of Ghazan Khan, the Ilkhanid king of Persia, where he served as a personal physician. Mas‘ud ibn Muhammad Sijzi's work on the diagnosis and treatment of diseases such as epilepsy and mental illness earned him recognition and respect from his contemporaries. His most notable achievement was the compilation of a comprehensive medical textbook, which was later adopted by scholars and physicians throughout the Islamic world. The legacy of Mas‘ud ibn Muhammad Sijzi can be seen in the continued practice of traditional Persian medicine, which remains an important part of the region's cultural heritage. Despite his significant contributions to the field of medicine, Mas‘ud ibn Muhammad Sijzi's life and work are not well documented in Western historical records, a reflection of the limited access to medical knowledge and scholarship in pre-modern Persia. Mas‘ud ibn Muhammad Sijzi's story serves as a reminder of the importance of preserving the knowledge and achievements of historical figures from diverse cultural backgrounds, and the need for greater understanding and appreciation of the historical and cultural context in which they lived and worked.
